page0.text:
The door closes.
As if convincing himself, the boy swore he'd protect the girl over and over. Then, he watched her fall asleep and left the room.

page1.text:
"...Ahh."
In the dim light, Sakura Matou heaves a pained sigh.
She hasn't been sleeping.
She only pretended to sleep to let the even more exhausted boy rest.

page2.text:
Besides, she can't sleep anymore.
If she does, she'll dream.
She'll watch something that looks like her kill people.
It terrifies her.
She doesn't remember what she dreamed last night.
She has no memory of what happened before she passed out in front of the house.

page3.text:
So, she's sure that if she falls asleep tonight, she'll never wake up again.
She'll lose her mind for good and betray the boy who embraced her.
The boy abandoned himself and chose to believe in the weak and dishonest Sakura Matou instead.
His conviction pains her. She knows that if she becomes the way she is in her dreams, she won't be able to face him again.

page4.text:
That's right.
She has broken his heart, and it can never be fixed.
So, she has to endure this.
She must stay awake and hold on to her mind as long as she can, so that she never has that dream again.
Even she has someone willing to protect her.
If there's even a shred left of her nasty, cowardly self...then Sakura Matou needs to hold onto it with all her might.

page5.text:
"I'm fine with that. But..."
...Some things can never go back to the way they were.
She's committed sins that she'll never be able to atone for.

page7.text:
He repeated that promise, knowing that there was no hope, no future.
The memory of it brings tears to her eyes.
Half an hour ago,
when he came into the room, she made up her mind.
She knows what it feels like when someone comes to kill her.
Right now, she's sensitive to hostility. She'd sense someone coming for her life even if she was asleep.

page8.text:
...But it was an empty bloodlust.
Not devoid of feeling,
but a pitiful void, like a gaping hole opened in his chest, allowing a cold breeze to flow through it.
She accepted that she would die here.
She thought it would be best if the boy was the one to stop her.

page9.text:
"...ry."
But she was too timid, too cowardly.
She told herself it was all right to die, but she couldn't stop herself from shaking.
She did it again.
She drove him into a corner with excuses convenient only for her.

page10.text:
"...orry."
He embraced her.
The boy embraced her, despite everything.
They both know they have no future.
He knew where his choice would lead, and he hugged her anyway.

page11.text:
She felt his determination.
His embrace told her that he would combine their sins and face the consequences together.

page12.text:
"Hngh... I'm sorry, Senpai..."
It made her sad.
She's always known that
he's someone who can do that.
...In the dusk-lit school yard,
she watched a stranger run, over and over.
The boy in the distance changed her whispers of "give up" into "good luck."

page13.text:
Her wish was born at that moment.
She wants to be with him.
She wants him to protect her.
She adored him without knowing why, and when her grandfather ordered her to go to the Emiya house, her dream came true.

page14.text: "I'll protect you, because I swore that I'd be on your side."

page15.text:
"Ngh...nngh...!"
This is the result of that promise.
He's going to keep breaking for the rest of his life.

page16.text:
"Sorry... I'm sorry, Senpai..."
She finally understands
why she looked up to him.
To the girl, the boy was beautiful.
She was pathetic, but he was different.
He was straightforward, and she wished for him to stay that way.

page17.text:
"But now, I've..."
...Yes, she's remembered.
She wanted to protect him.
I wanted to protect him.
That awkward, honest person she saw in the yard that afternoon was precious to her, and she wanted to protect him.
"I...broke him."

page18.text:
That's all she ever wanted.
So, why...
Why did she do this to him?

page19.text:
...And so,
during a span of time which would've been interrupted if she hadn't had her mind focused, she made her final choice.

page20.text:
"Are you there, Rider?"
She calls out into the darkness.
"..."
A woman appears out of thin air, like a ghost.
She is Rider, Sakura Matou's Servant.

page21.text:
"...I knew it. Have you been protecting me?"
"Yes. I would have killed him if he raised a hand against you."
...
She sighs. That was a close call.
Rider would give priority to her Master's life.
She only judges people based on whether they threaten her Master or not.
Meaning that a moment ago, Shirou Emiya was undoubtedly Rider's enemy.

page22.text:
"...Don't hurt Senpai, Rider. I won't forgive you if you do."
"My role is to protect you, Sakura. If he becomes your enemy, then I must fulfill my duty. I will protect Sakura Matou, no matter what happens to you."
"...Even if I'm no longer myself?"

page23.text:
Rider doesn't say anything.
That's the answer Sakura fears the most.
Indeed...
Even if Shirou Emiya is Sakura Matou's ally,
Rider will view him as an enemy to be defeated if she judges him a threat to Sakura.

page24.text:
"..."
The girl sits up and clenches her fist.
...She isn't angry at Rider.
She's just afraid that her hypothesis might turn out to be true.

page27.text:
"...I'll stop Grandfather.
This is a Matou problem... It's overdue, but I won't cause Shirou any more trouble."
She declares her next move, holding back a cough.
Her eyes burn bright in the darkness.
Their frail glow marks the determination of a mage.
